## Overview

**VetResearchLMM** gives the data sets and every analysis of Duchateau,
Janssen and Rowlands (1998), *Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with
Applications in Veterinary Research* (ILRI, Nairobi), with its own
engine for linear mixed models that gives the results the book prints
from SAS PROC MIXED and PROC GLM.

- [`vlm_fit()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_fit.md):
  REML, ML or Type 3 (moment) estimation; random variance components,
  random coefficients
  ([`vlm_random()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_random.md),
  VC or UN) and residual structures
  ([`vlm_repeated()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_random.md):
  CS, AR(1), SP(POW), UN); the fixed-effects solution in the
  overparameterised coding; Type 3 or Type 1 tests with containment,
  residual, between-within, Satterthwaite or Kenward-Roger degrees of
  freedom; fit statistics;
- [`vlm_lsmeans()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_lsmeans.md),
  [`vlm_estimate()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_estimate.md),
  [`vlm_contrast()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_estimate.md):
  least-squares means with Tukey, Bonferroni or Sidak comparisons,
  estimates in the broad and narrow inference spaces, and F tests of
  contrasts;
- [`vlm_blup()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_blup.md):
  best linear unbiased predictions of random effects;
- [`vlm_ems()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_ems.md):
  the analysis of variance with expected mean squares and synthesised F
  tests;
- [`vlm_compare()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_compare.md):
  information criteria and likelihood ratio tests of covariance
  structures;
- [`vlm_interpret()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_interpret.md),
  [`vlm_cite()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_cite.md),
  [`vlm_app()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_app.md):
  plain-language interpretation, references and a shiny application in
  which every example of the book loads with one click.

The help pages
[`?Examp1.3.2`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp1.3.2.md)
to
[`?Examp3.3`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp3.3.md)
give the SAS program of each example with the same analysis in R. The
package reproduces 115 of the 116 numbers of the book that it checks;
the other one is printed truncated (3.685 for 3.6855). Version 2.0.0
keeps the data sets, the help topics and
[`emmeans_mixed_model()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/emmeans_mixed_model.md)
and
[`report_mixed_model()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/report_mixed_model.md)
of version 1.1.0, adds the data sets of Examples 1.2.2, 1.2.3 and 1.2.6,
and corrects three typing errors in `ex33`.

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("VetResearchLMM")
# development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("myaseen208/VetResearchLMM")
```

## Quick start

The split-plot experiment of Example 1.2.5 (drugs given to herds within
regions, doses to animals within herds):

``` r

library(VetResearchLMM)
fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
fm
```

``` R
Linear mixed model: Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
Estimation: REML; denominator df: satterth; converged after 6 iterations
Random: Region; Region:Drug

Covariance parameter estimates
   parameter subject estimate     se      z      p
      Region            5.151  3.739  1.378 0.0842
 Region:Drug           0.3870  1.022 0.3788 0.3524
    Residual            2.096 0.9375  2.236 0.0127

Fit statistics
                statistic   value
    -2 Res Log Likelihood 92.3786
  AIC (smaller is better) 98.3786
 AICC (smaller is better) 99.8786
  BIC (smaller is better) 101.366

Solution for fixed effects
      effect     level estimate     se    df      t        p
 (Intercept)              17.13  1.128 8.208  15.19  < 1e-04
        Drug   BERENIL    7.150 0.9098 11.82  7.859  < 1e-04
        Drug   samorin        0                            .
        dose         h    4.350 0.8359 10.00  5.204 0.000399
        dose         l        0                            .
   Drug:dose BERENIL h   -3.183  1.182 10.00 -2.693 0.022594
   Drug:dose BERENIL l        0                            .
   Drug:dose samorin h        0                            .
   Drug:dose samorin l        0                            .

Type 3 tests of fixed effects
    effect num_df den_df     F        p
      Drug      1  5.000 64.58 0.000483
      dose      1  10.00 21.78 0.000886
 Drug:dose      1  10.00 7.251 0.022594

Sources: Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998); Patterson and Thompson (1971);
Gilmour, Thompson and Cullis (1995); Littell, Milliken, Stroup and Wolfinger
(1996); Satterthwaite (1946); Giesbrecht and Burns (1985); Fai and Cornelius
(1996). Full references: vlm_cite(x).
```

``` r

vlm_interpret(
    x     = fm
  , alpha = 0.05
  , top   = 3L
  )
```

``` R
Linear mixed model

Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose, fitted by REML with 3 covariance parameters.

Findings:
- Of the total variance 7.63, 67.5% is due to Region, 5.1% is due to
  Region:Drug, 27.5% is due to the residual (within) variation.
- Significant at the 0.05 level: Drug (F = 64.6 on 1 and 5 df, p = 0.00048);
  dose (F = 21.8 on 1 and 10 df, p = 0.00089); Drug:dose (F = 7.25 on 1 and
  10 df, p = 0.023).

Recommendations:
- The interaction Drug:dose is significant: compare the levels of one factor
  within each level of the other (vlm_lsmeans() of the interaction, or
  vlm_estimate()) rather than main-effect means.
- Report means with standard errors in the broad inference space
  (vlm_lsmeans()); use vlm_estimate() with `random` for the narrow space of
  the observed levels.

Sources:
- Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models.
  An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International
  Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi. ISBN 92-9146-038-9.
- Patterson, H. D. and Thompson, R. (1971). Recovery of inter-block
  information when block sizes are unequal. Biometrika, 58(3), 545-554.
  doi:10.1093/biomet/58.3.545
- Gilmour, A. R., Thompson, R. and Cullis, B. R. (1995). Average information
  REML: an efficient algorithm for variance parameter estimation in linear
  mixed models. Biometrics, 51(4), 1440-1450. doi:10.2307/2533274
- Littell, R. C., Milliken, G. A., Stroup, W. W. and Wolfinger, R. D. (1996).
  SAS System for Mixed Models. SAS Institute, Cary, NC.
- Satterthwaite, F. E. (1946). An approximate distribution of estimates of
  variance components. Biometrics Bulletin, 2(6), 110-114.
  doi:10.2307/3002019
- Giesbrecht, F. G. and Burns, J. C. (1985). Two-stage analysis based on a
  mixed model: large-sample asymptotic theory and small-sample simulation
  results. Biometrics, 41(2), 477-486. doi:10.2307/2530872
- Fai, A. H.-T. and Cornelius, P. L. (1996). Approximate F-tests of multiple
  degree of freedom hypotheses in generalized least squares analyses of
  unbalanced split-plot experiments. Journal of Statistical Computation and
  Simulation, 54(4), 363-378. doi:10.1080/00949659608811740
```

``` r

lm1 <-
  vlm_lsmeans(
      fit    = fm
    , specs  = ~ Drug:dose
    , at     = NULL
    , diff   = TRUE
    , adjust = "tukey"
    , level  = 0.95
    )
plot(x = lm1)
```

## Learn more

- Vignettes: `browseVignettes("VetResearchLMM")`, starting with
  `VetResearchLMM_01_getting_started`; PDF versions on the site.
- Site: <https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/>
- Notation:
  [`vlm_notation()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_notation.md)
- References of the methods behind a result:
  [`vlm_cite()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_cite.md)

## Citation

``` R
Yaseen M, Duchateau L, Janssen P, Rowlands J (2026). _VetResearchLMM:
Linear Mixed Models: An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary
Research_. R package version 2.0.0,
<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=VetResearchLMM>.
```

BibTeX:

``` R
@Manual{VetResearchLMM,
  title = {{VetResearchLMM}: Linear Mixed Models: An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research},
  author = {Muhammad Yaseen and Luc Duchateau and Paul Janssen and John Rowlands},
  year = {2026},
  note = {R package version 2.0.0},
  url = {https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=VetResearchLMM},
}
```

Please also cite the book: `citation("VetResearchLMM")` lists it with
the package, and `vlm_cite(x)` gives the references of a single result.

# Package index

## Models

- [`vlm_fit()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_fit.md)
  : Fit a linear mixed model
- [`vlm_random()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_random.md)
  [`vlm_repeated()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_random.md)
  : Random-effects and residual covariance structures
- [`vlm_ems()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_ems.md)
  : Analysis of variance with expected mean squares
- [`vlm_compare()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_compare.md)
  : Compare fitted models

## Inference

- [`vlm_lsmeans()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_lsmeans.md)
  : Least-squares means
- [`vlm_estimate()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_estimate.md)
  [`vlm_contrast()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_estimate.md)
  : Estimates and contrasts of fixed (and random) effects
- [`vlm_blup()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_blup.md)
  : Best linear unbiased predictions of the random effects

## The examples of the book

- [`Examp1.3.2`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp1.3.2.md)
  : Example 1.3.2: expected mean squares in the fixed and the mixed
  model
- [`Examp2.2.1.7`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.2.1.7.md)
  : Example 2.2.1.7: one-way analysis of variance, an estimate and a
  contrast
- [`Examp2.3.2`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.3.2.md)
  : Example 2.3.2: the mixed model descriptions of Chapter 2
- [`Examp2.4.2.2`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.4.2.2.md)
  : Example 2.4.2.2: ML and REML estimates of variance components
- [`Examp2.4.3.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.4.3.1.md)
  : Example 2.4.3.1: best linear unbiased prediction of sire effects
- [`Examp2.5.1.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.5.1.1.md)
  : Example 2.5.1.1: generalised least-squares estimates of the fixed
  effects
- [`Examp2.5.2.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.5.2.1.md)
  : Example 2.5.2.1: cell means as estimable functions
- [`Examp2.5.3.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.5.3.1.md)
  : Example 2.5.3.1: confidence intervals with Satterthwaite degrees of
  freedom
- [`Examp2.5.4.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.5.4.1.md)
  : Example 2.5.4.1: broad and narrow inference spaces
- [`Examp2.6.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp2.6.1.md)
  : Example 2.6.1: F tests of general linear hypotheses
- [`Examp3.1`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp3.1.md)
  : Example 3.1: a designed experiment with doses nested in drug and a
  covariate
- [`Examp3.2`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp3.2.md)
  : Example 3.2: sires nested in breed, heritability and breed
  comparisons
- [`Examp3.3`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/Examp3.3.md)
  : Example 3.3: covariance structures for repeated measures

## Data sets of the book

- [`ex121`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex121.md) :
  Example 1.2.1: comparing three doses of a drug
- [`ex122`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex122.md) :
  Example 1.2.2: comparing two doses of a drug in a randomised block
  design
- [`ex123`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex123.md) :
  Example 1.2.3: comparing two drugs with herds as experimental units
- [`ex124`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex124.md) :
  Example 1.2.4: two drugs at two doses with two sizes of experimental
  units
- [`ex125`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex125.md) :
  Example 1.2.5: two drugs at two doses in a split-plot design
- [`ex126`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex126.md) :
  Example 1.2.6: variation in ELISA data
- [`ex127`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex127.md) :
  Example 1.2.7: helminth resistance in sheep
- [`ex31`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex31.md) :
  Example 3.1: two drugs and their doses, herds nested in drug (part of
  the data)
- [`ex32`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex32.md) :
  Example 3.2: weaning weights of lambs by breed and sire (part of the
  data)
- [`ex33`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/ex33.md) :
  Example 3.3: breed differences in susceptibility to trypanosomosis

- [`vlm_app()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_app.md)
  [`vlm_app_object()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_app.md)

## Version 1.1.0

Kept, and extended to vlm_fit() results.

- [`emmeans_mixed_model()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/emmeans_mixed_model.md)
  : Estimated marginal means for a fitted mixed model
- [`report_mixed_model()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/report_mixed_model.md)
  : Report a fitted mixed model

## Utilities

- [`vlm_cite()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_cite.md)
  : References of a result or of the package
- [`vlm_theme()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_theme.md)
  : ggplot2 theme of VetResearchLMM
- [`vlm_save()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_save.md)
  : Save a figure (vector PDF by default)
- [`vlm_notation()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_notation.md)
  : Notation of VetResearchLMM
- [`vlm_reference()`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/vlm_reference.md)
  : Published values used by the tests and vignettes
- [`VetResearchLMM`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/VetResearchLMM-package.md)
  [`VetResearchLMM-package`](https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/reference/VetResearchLMM-package.md)
  : VetResearchLMM: Linear Mixed Models with Applications in Veterinary
  Research
